column2: Retain Amaziah son of Judah's Joash becoming king in the second year of Israel's Joash son of Jehoahaz. The same-named fathers and contemporary rulers remain distinguished by their genealogies and kingdoms.
Retain age twenty-five, twenty-nine years in Jerusalem and Joadin from Jerusalem as mother. The maternal name is not silently standardized to a familiar parallel form.
Retain right conduct qualified by not like David and by conformity to his father Joash. Father serves different dynastic and immediate senses in the two comparisons; neither comparison is dropped.

Retain the high-place exception, failure to remove them and continued sacrifice/incense. Only introduces the exception rather than restricting all wrongdoing to a single action beyond what the verse states.

Retain the kingdom becoming firm in his hand and action against the servants who struck his father. Struck down is supported by the surrounding death and killers context, not treated as an invariant translation of every occurrence of strike.

Retain sparing the killers' sons and the Moses-law citation with reciprocal father/son non-substitution and each person's own sins. Only is supported by the restrictive construction; no collective punishment is inserted into the quotation.

Retain ten thousand Edomites at Gaimela, capture of the Rock and naming Kathoel to this day. Rock represents the selected Petra term without deciding whether a geographical proper-name spelling is preferable; no familiar alternate place names are substituted.

Retain Amaziah's messengers, Joash's two-generation genealogy and invitation to face one another. The challenge's military force emerges from the exchange; no explicit duel between the two individuals is added.

Retain the Lebanon thornbush and cedar, daughter-for-son marriage request and plural wild animals trampling the thornbush. The fable remains in direct speech, with no explanation of every character's royal counterpart added.

Retain the emphatic Edom victory, heart's elevation, glory at home, contention in wickedness and predicted fall of king and Judah. The selected in your wickedness is not changed into merely inviting trouble without review.
column3: Does en kakia sou denote wickedness or adverse consequences here, and how should the glory-at-home imperative sound in natural English?

column2: Retain Amaziah's refusal to listen and the kings facing one another at Baithsamys in Judah. This repeats the face-to-face wording from the challenge rather than supplying a separate battle description here.
Retain Judah stumbling before Israel and each man fleeing to his own dwelling. Stumbled preserves the defeat image; the text does not give a casualty count.

Retain both royal genealogies, Amaziah's capture at Baithsamys and four hundred cubits of Jerusalem's wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate. The length and named endpoints are not converted into approximate modern measurements.

Retain gold, silver, all vessels in the two treasury locations and sons of the mixed unions, followed by return to Samaria. The unusual human category remains unresolved rather than being silently translated as hostages.
column3: Does sons of the symmixes denote hostages, intermarriage offspring or another dependent group, and what lexical evidence distinguishes these readings?

column2: Retain Joash's deeds, might, warfare with Amaziah and Israel's chronicles reference. In this context fought with is naturally hostile, but the summary is not expanded into new episodes.
Retain Joash's death, burial in Samaria with Israel's kings and his son Jeroboam succeeding. This notice differs from 13:13 and is not harmonized by deleting its burial clause.
Retain Amaziah outliving Israel's Joash by fifteen years, with both kings' fathers and kingdoms. The statement measures survival after a death, not simply total reign length.
Retain Amaziah's remaining deeds, everything done and the Judah chronicles question. No presentative is supplied where this selected formula lacks one.
Retain conspiracy in Jerusalem, flight to Lachish, pursuit sent there and death there. The conspirators remain unnamed and the repeated destination is preserved.
Retain conveyance on plural horses and burial in Jerusalem with fathers in David's city. A chariot or funeral procession is not supplied to explain the plural mounts.
Retain all Judah's people taking sixteen-year-old Azariah and making him king instead of Amaziah his father. The age remains parenthetical, and the people's agency is explicit.
Retain Azariah's building of Ailoth and restoration to Judah after the king's death. The preceding father is the natural referent of the king; no date or maritime role is added.

Retain Jeroboam son of Joash's forty-one years in Samaria, beginning in Amaziah's fifteenth year. The repeated Joash names are not conflated, and the figures are left unharmonized with later accession dates.

Retain the evil evaluation and not turning from any of Jeroboam son of Nebat's sins. Any appropriately conveys the selected all-sins phrase under negation and agrees with the proposed negative-scope rendering in 13:11.

Retain shifted for the selected boundary verb, Aimath-to-Arabah range and the oracle through Jonah son of Amathi from Gethchober. The selected verb is not silently replaced by restored; the exact boundary action remains unresolved.
column3: Does apestesen here mean moved, set apart or restored by contextual extension, and should shifted be retained after lexical review?

column2: Retain very bitter humiliation, few, hemmed in, impoverished and abandoned, with no helper. The positive statement that a few remain is not replaced with no one confined or free; each selected descriptor remains.

Retain the Lord not declaring the erasure of Israel's seed and saving through Jeroboam son of Joash. Seed differs from a familiar name formulation, and the king's earlier evil evaluation is not erased to simplify divine deliverance.

Retain Jeroboam's deeds, power and wars, and restoration of Damascus and Aimath to Judah in Israel. The difficult kingdom relation remains rather than being silently rewritten as recovery for Israel alone.
column3: How do to Judah and in Israel attach to the restoration clause, and does the selected wording imply a historical claim different from familiar parallels?

column2: Retain Jeroboam's death with Israel's kings followed by Azariah son of Amaziah reigning in his father's place. The abrupt change of royal line is selected; Zechariah is not substituted to create a conventional succession notice.
Retain Azariah son of Amaziah's accession in Jeroboam's twenty-seventh year. The date is not reconciled by changing the earlier Azariah notice or supplying a co-regency theory in the text.
Retain age sixteen, fifty-two years in Jerusalem and mother Chalia from Jerusalem. Chalia is the inherited selected form and is not silently expanded to another maternal name.
Retain right conduct in the Lord's eyes according to all his father Amaziah did. The comparison is stated without importing another book's temple-entry episode.
Retain the high-place exception and continued sacrifices/incense. The repetition of this royal evaluation formula remains; it is not abbreviated merely because it appeared in the previous chapter.

Retain the Lord touching the king, leprosy until death, reigning in the house of Apphousoth and Jotham's palace/governing role. Reigned is the selected verb, not merely lived; the unknown house term is not confidently rendered isolation house.
column3: What does apphousoth denote, and how does the king's continued reigning relate to Jotham's judging without a supplied constitutional reconstruction?

column2: Retain Azariah's deeds, everything done, Behold and Judah's chronicles question. The presentative is explicit in this formula and contrasts with nearby formulas lacking it.
Retain death and burial with fathers in David's city and Jotham's succession. The selected account does not add a separate burial field or exclusion from royal tombs.
Retain Zechariah son of Jeroboam's accession in Azariah's thirty-eighth year and six months in Samaria. The short reign is months, not years.
Retain the fathers' evil example and failure to leave Jeroboam son of Nebat's sins. The ancestral plural remains, without identifying each preceding king individually.

Retain Sellum son of Jabis and Keblaam as two participants, with plural conspiracy, striking and killing, followed by Sellum's singular succession. Keblaam is not replaced with a before-the-people phrase from another textual form.
column3: Is Keblaam best retained as a participant's name in this selected construction, and what apparatus evidence would be needed before revising it?

column2: Retain the presentative declaration that Zechariah's remaining deeds are written. This is a statement, not the rhetorical question used in some other royal summaries.
Retain the Lord's word to Jehu about sons to the fourth generation and explicit fulfillment. Fourth generation is a contextual dynastic rendering; no further successors are promised in this clause.

Propose reigned for a month for reigned a month of days, giving the pleonastic temporal expression natural English. The repeated accession statement, thirty-ninth year and Samaria remain; no fixed thirty-day duration is asserted.

Retain Manaem son of Gaddi, departure from Tharsila, arrival at Samaria and killing Sellum there. The selected verse does not add and became king at its end, so that familiar succession clause is not inserted.
Retain Sellum's deeds, his conspiracy and the presentative chronicles statement. The specific conspiracy is included rather than collapsed into a generic royal record reference.

Retain Thersa, everything within it, territory from Thersa, refusal to open, attack and violence against pregnant women. The repeated Thersa is not harmonized to Tiphsah or another familiar place; no extra motive beyond the refused opening is supplied.
Retain Manaem son of Gaddi's ten years in Samaria and accession in Azariah's thirty-ninth year. The same year as Sellum's brief reign is preserved without an added month-by-month chronology.
Retain the evil evaluation and negative any-sin scope for Jeroboam son of Nebat. The next unit, rather than this one, begins in his days; the stored boundary remains.

Retain Phul king of the Assyrians, invasion, one thousand silver talents and the purpose that his hand be with Manaem. The hand-support idiom is not expanded into an absent explicit statement about confirming his kingdom.

Retain the levy on Israel's mighty-in-strength men, fifty shekels each, payment to Assyria and the king's withdrawal without remaining. Wealth/status is inferred by the levy context but not substituted for the selected strength phrase as settled terminology.
Retain Manaem's remaining deeds, all he did, Behold and the Israel chronicles question. The formula's question form differs from Sellum's preceding declarative notice.
Retain Manaem's death with fathers and Phakeias his son's succession. No burial location is supplied in this shorter notice.
Retain Phakeias son of Manaem's accession in Azariah's fiftieth year and two-year reign in Samaria. Phakeias remains distinct from Phakee in the following conspiracy.
Retain evil in the Lord's eyes and failure to turn from Jeroboam son of Nebat's sins. The selected phrase lacks all here, so the inherited wording appropriately does not insert any of all these sins.

Retain Phakee son of Romelias, his officer role, attack before the royal house, Argob and Aria, and fifty men from the four hundred. The two named associates' attachment is unresolved; four hundred is not replaced with Gileadites.
column3: Does third-ranking adequately express tristates, and are Argob/Aria victims or accomplices in the with-phrases? The selected fifty-from-four-hundred figure remains independent of that issue.

column2: Retain Phakeias's remaining deeds and all he did in a presentative chronicles statement. The victim's name is not accidentally changed to the new ruler Phakee.

Retain Phakee son of Romelias's twenty-year reign from Azariah's fifty-second year. The figure remains despite later chronological difficulties; no historical solution is inserted into the translation.
Retain evil before the Lord and not turning from any Jeroboam son of Nebat sins. The all-sins expression under negation is naturally represented by any, consistent with verse 18.

Retain Thaglathphellasar and all seven named areas: Ain, Abelbaithamaacha, Janoch, Kenez, Asor, Gilead and Galilee, followed by all Naphtali's land and deportation to the Assyrians. Kenez is not silently replaced with Kedesh.
Retain Hoshea son of Ela's conspiracy, killing and succession in Jotham son of Azariah's twentieth year. The twentieth year is not changed to fit Jotham's sixteen-year total in verse 33.
Retain Phakee's remaining deeds and all he did in the presentative chronicles statement. The summary closes the deposed king's notice without an added burial account.
Retain Jotham son of Azariah's accession in Phakee son of Romelias's second year. The two kingdoms and genealogies remain clear, without attempting to reconcile every regnal overlap.

Retain age twenty-five, sixteen years in Jerusalem and Jerusa daughter of Sadok. The sixteen-year total remains alongside the earlier twentieth-year synchronism; the maternal genealogy is not omitted.
Retain right conduct according to his father Ozias. Ozias is the selected form here, distinct from Azariah in the accession notice; the text is not globally standardized to a single name.

Retain the high-place exception and continuing sacrifices/incense, then construction of the upper gate of the Lord's house. Upper is not expanded into a compass direction or an architectural reconstruction.
Retain Jotham's remaining deeds and everything done in the Judah chronicles question. This selected formula lacks Behold, so the inherited absence remains.

Retain the Lord beginning to send Raasson king of Syria and Phakee son of Romelias against Judah. The divine agency remains explicit; the names are not standardized to forms in later chapters without separate review.
Retain Jotham's death and burial with fathers in David's city and Ahaz his son's succession. The dynastic father language for David is preserved without an explanatory genealogy in the verse.
